log: Working out who would actually buy this
Rechecking product fit for the same audiences; market evidence is retained

Coverage gaps and failures: (1) Direct buyer-voice forum threads were hard to surface — three attempts at Reddit and Hacker News practitioner threads on freelance multi-client analytics and Ghost/newsletter publishers returned vendor comparison pages instead, so the freelancer segment leans on the existence of a reporting-tool market rather than quoted complaints. (2) No churn evidence found: searches for people who left or cancelled Fathom turned up only review-site remarks that it is 'expensive for what you get' and costs more per pageview than Plausible past 1M views, with no first-person account — real churn reasons remain unknown. (3) Security posture unverified: a search for Fathom Analytics SOC 2/BAA returned results for an unrelated AI meeting-notes company also called Fathom, so treat any certification claim as unconfirmed and do not reuse those hits. (4) No named EU public-sector or university procurement decision was found, so the institutional variant of the compliance buyer is unsupported and was not proposed as a separate segment. (5) Search scope was left empty, so no geography was imposed; German-language vocabulary was tried once and returned agency listicles rather than buyer discussion. (6) Population counts are unknown throughout, fit is left at zero, and assessment fields are left at defaults for separate validation. (7) The Shopify candidate has no documented install path in the supplied capability catalogue — verify before using it. (8) One source (clickport) is a vendor-adjacent guide and one (levelup) is a practitioner essay; both should be read as advocacy, and the consent-loss percentages they cite differ widely and need independent checking.
